page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 219.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 54.69 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 262 GB volume, and the instance is premium storage capable. No graphics processing units are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates that the M8-4ms prioritizes memory capacity over raw processing speed and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1035.08 falls in the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 2724.76 is in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 151.25 GB/sec and an uncached large block write speed of 17.19 GB/sec. Similarly, the Geekbench single-core score of 885.0 and multi-core score of 1970.0 both rank in the bottom 10%. These results highlight a clear tradeoff: the server provides an exceptionally large memory footprint but exhibits lower computational and memory bandwidth performance per resource unit.

Given its hardware profile, the M8-4ms is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require large datasets to reside in RAM but do not demand high CPU throughput. Suitable workloads include large-scale in-memory caching, database operations with low transactional frequency, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for consolidating memory-bound tasks, though it is less cost-effective for compute-heavy or high-throughput data processing due to its lower benchmark performance relative to its hardware class.
